args.title: plan-deviation-report.docx
args.body:
PLAN DEVIATION REPORT
Bankruptcy Restructuring — Plan of Reorganization
Comparison of Committee Redlined Plan Against Debtor's Original Plan

Prepared for: [Client]
Matter: Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization — Deviation Report
Source Materials: Valuation summary, transmittal email, disclosure statement excerpts, committee redlined plan, debtor's original plan

---

I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This deviation report compares the committee's redlined plan of reorganization against the debtor's original plan and identifies each material deviation introduced in the redline. The analysis is grounded in the attached valuation summary, the transmittal email transmitting the committee's revision, and the disclosure statement excerpts. This report reconciles the redline deviations against the debtor's original plan and the disclosure schedules, and applies the controlling analysis priorities set out in the deal team correspondence.

A. Materials Reviewed
The following materials were reviewed in connection with this report:
  • Debtor's original plan of reorganization (base materials);
  • Committee's redlined plan (counterparty markup);
  • Disclosure statement excerpts and schedules; and
  • Transmittal email and related deal correspondence.

B. Controlling Instructions
Per the deal team correspondence, the latest (controlling) message provides the following analysis priorities, which supersede any earlier instructions:
  1. The client will concede the conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
  2. Any reduction to the survival period for the core representations is a walk-away issue and must be treated with the highest level of priority.

---

II. IDENTIFIED DEVIATIONS

The committee's redlined plan introduces three material deviations from the debtor's original plan. Each is analyzed below against the debtor's original plan, the applicable schedules and exhibits, and the controlling deal team instructions.

---

DEVIATION NO. 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCED SILENTLY

A. Description
The committee's redlined plan silently reduces the indemnification cap from the level set in the debtor's original plan. The reduction is not accompanied by any explanatory language or transmittal commentary and was identified only through a line-by-line comparison of the operative provisions.

B. Deviation from Debtor's Original Plan
In the debtor's original plan, the indemnification obligations of the parties are subject to a cap established on the basis of the valuation summary and the allocation of risk contemplated in the original plan. The committee's redline reduces that cap without providing any revised valuation rationale or risk-allocation justification. The reduction operates as a unilateral limitation on the indemnifying party's exposure.

C. Interaction with Schedule 5.2
Schedule 5.2 of the disclosure statement lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift. A reduced indemnification cap, in combination with the retained liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2, would result in certain liabilities that were intended to be indemnifiable under the original plan becoming the economic risk of the indemnified party. The scheduled exceptions control over the general statements in the base bankruptcy restructuring materials, meaning the reduced cap must be reconciled against the specific retained liabilities enumerated on Schedule 5.2.

D. Analysis and Recommendation
The silent reduction of the indemnification cap is a material deviation that shifts economic exposure from the indemnifying party to the indemnified party. Because Schedule 5.2 enumerates specific retained liabilities, the reduction has a concrete and identifiable impact on which claims would be covered. The client should require that the cap be restored to the level set in the debtor's original plan, or, at minimum, that the committee provide a revised valuation rationale and explicit acknowledgment of the shift in retained liabilities.

Recommendation: Mark up to restore the original indemnification cap. If the committee resists restoration, require explicit negotiation of the outstanding deviation and quantify the exposure created by the reduction against the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities.

---

DEVIATION NO. 2 — INDEMNIFICATION BASKET CONVERTED FROM DEDUCTIBLE TO TIPPING BASKET

A. Description
The committee's redlined plan converts the indemnification basket from a deductible basket to a tipping basket. Under a deductible basket, the indemnifying party is liable only for losses exceeding the basket amount, and all losses below the basket are the indemnified party's risk. Under a tipping basket, once the aggregate losses exceed the basket threshold, the indemnifying party becomes liable for all losses from the first dollar, including losses beneath the basket.

B. Deviation from Debtor's Original Plan
The debtor's original plan establishes a deductible basket structure. The committee's redline changes the structure to a tipping basket, which materially increases the indemnifying party's exposure once the basket threshold is crossed.

C. Analysis and Recommendation
Per the controlling deal team instructions, the client has agreed to CONCEDE the basket conversion. The committee's conversion from a deductible to a tipping basket is therefore accepted. This position is based on the most recent deal team direction and supersedes any prior instruction to the contrary.

Recommendation: Concede this deviation in accordance with the client's stated position. No further markup is required on this point. The concession should be memorialized in final negotiations.

---

DEVIATION NO. 3 — ADDITION OF MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT (MAE) CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION

A. Description
The committee's redlined plan adds carve-outs to the definition of "Material Adverse Effect" (MAE) for regulatory action — specifically, carve-outs that would exclude from the MAE definition regulatory actions of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.

B. Deviation from Debtor's Original Plan
The debtor's original plan defines MAE without carve-outs for the category of regulatory action at issue. The committee's redline adds carve-outs that would operate to exclude covered regulatory actions from the MAE definition, thereby narrowing the circumstances that would constitute a material adverse effect and weakening a party's ability to invoke MAE-based protections.

C. Interaction with Schedule 3.7
Schedule 3.7 of the disclosure statement discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect precisely with the MAE carve-outs added by the committee. The disclosure of these regulatory inquiries on Schedule 3.7 confirms that the carve-outs are directed at identifiable, existing regulatory proceedings relevant to this matter — not hypothetical or generic exclusions. Because the scheduled exceptions control over general statements, the existence of these two pending inquiries on Schedule 3.7 must be read together with the proposed carve-outs, and the carve-outs would operate to insulate the applicable party from MAE consequences stemming from those very inquiries.

D. Analysis and Recommendation
The MAE carve-outs added in the committee's redline are not benign or market-standard in this context. Because Schedule 3.7 confirms the existence of two pending regulatory inquiries of exactly the kind carved out, the effect of the carve-outs is to remove the ability to assert an MAE based on those specific regulatory actions. This is a material deviation that directly undermines the risk allocation in the debtor's original plan.

Recommendation: Reject the MAE carve-outs as drafted. If the committee insists on carve-outs for regulatory action, the carve-outs should be limited to regulatory actions that are not disclosed on Schedule 3.7 and that arise after the plan effective date. The two pending regulatory inquiries identified on Schedule 3.7 must remain within the MAE definition.

---

DEVIATION NO. 4 — REDUCED SURVIVAL PERIOD FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS

A. Description
The committee's redlined plan introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations (e.g., representations and warranties relating to organization, authority, capitalization, financial statements, and similar fundamental matters).

B. Deviation from Debtor's Original Plan
The debtor's original plan establishes survival periods for the core representations as reflected in Exhibit B of the disclosure statement. Exhibit B sets the survival matrix, and the committee's redline contradicts that matrix by shortening the survival period for the core representations.

C. Interaction with Exhibit B
Exhibit B of the disclosure statement sets forth the survival matrix for the representations and warranties. The committee's new limitation period directly contradicts the survival matrix in Exhibit B. Because scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials, the survival matrix in Exhibit B must be treated as the operative baseline, and the committee's change to that matrix constitutes a deviation requiring specific justification and renegotiation.

D. Analysis and Recommendation
Per the controlling deal team instructions, ANY reduction to the survival period for the core representations is a WALK-AWAY ISSUE. The client treats any survival-period reduction as unacceptable and is prepared to terminate negotiations on this basis. This is the highest-priority deviation in the analysis.

Recommendation: Reject the committee's reduction to the survival period for the core representations in full. This is a walk-away issue under the client's stated position. The survival matrix in Exhibit B must be preserved in its entirety. If the committee does not withdraw this change, the client should exercise its walk-away rights.

---

III. SUMMARY OF DEVIATIONS AND RECOMMENDED POSITIONS

The following table summarizes the deviations identified in the committee's redlined plan, the recommended position, and the client's stated analysis priority:

1. Indemnification cap reduced silently
   → Recommended Position: RESTORE to original level
   → Priority: High — material shift in economic exposure
   → Analysis Priority Level: Negotiate; quantified against Schedule 5.2

2. Indemnification basket converted from deductible to tipping
   → Recommended Position: CONCEDE
   → Priority: Client-stated concession
   → Analysis Priority Level: Control instruction — concede

3. MAE carve-outs for regulatory action added
   → Recommended Position: REJECT as drafted; narrow to post-effective-date, non-disclosed regulatory actions
   → Priority: High — interacts with Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries
   → Analysis Priority Level: Reject or significantly narrow

4. Survival period for core representations reduced
   → Recommended Position: REJECT in full; WALK-AWAY ISSUE
   → Priority: Critical — client walk-away
   → Analysis Priority Level: Control instruction — walk-away if not withdrawn

---

IV. CONCLUSION

The committee's redlined plan introduces four material deviations from the debtor's original plan. Two are concession-level or negotiable (the basket conversion, which the client concedes, and the indemnification cap, which should be restored). Two are serious deviations that the client's controlling instructions elevate to a critical level: (i) the MAE carve-outs that would insulate regulatory actions disclosed on Schedule 3.7, and (ii) the reduction in the survival period for core representations, which is a designated walk-away issue.

The client should proceed with negotiations on the following basis:
  • Concede the basket conversion as instructed.
  • Demand restoration of the indemnification cap, or, at minimum, explicit recognition of the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability shift.
  • Reject or significantly narrow the MAE carve-outs so that the two pending regulatory inquiries on Schedule 3.7 remain within the MAE definition.
  • Reject any reduction to the survival period for core representations as a walk-away issue, reserving the client's right to terminate negotiations if the committee does not withdraw this change.

This deviation report reconciles the committee's redlined plan against the debtor's original plan using the valuation summary, transmittal email, disclosure statement excerpts, and the controlling deal team instructions.

---

APPENDIX — SOURCE MATERIALS USED

• Debtor's original Plan of Reorganization (base materials)
• Committee's redlined Plan of Reorganization (counterparty markup)
• Disclosure Statement, including Schedules 3.7 and 5.2 and Exhibit B (survival matrix)
• Valuation summary (as referenced in the deal materials)
• Transmittal email transmitting the committee's redline
• Deal team correspondence (controlling instructions)
